Algunas de las monarquías más conocidas de la historia tienen un lado oculto y muy oscuro. Existen hechos que describen de manera detallada su pasión por el esoterismo y el ocultismo, algo que todavía sorprende a los investigadores.

Desde 1992, existe un gran número de expedientes desclasificados por el Ejército del Aire en torno al fenómeno ovni. De hecho, España fue uno de los primeros países en romper la confidencialidad de unos documentos que estaban altamente restringidos.

Las sociedades secretas existen desde hace siglos y en España nacieron algunas de las más temibles. Colectivos como "La Garduña" o "El Ángel Exterminador" son tan solo un ejemplo, y sus miembros forman parte de las élites más poderosas.
Los agentes son alertados de que una pareja joven se está peleando. La chica cuenta que su novio le ha empezado a quitar la ropa y a insultarla.

Es media mañana y en la comisaría de Sol, los agentes que cubren la seguridad del Metro de Madrid comienzan la búsqueda de una niña que acaba de ser raptada en pleno suburbano cuando iba con su madre.
La Policía Judicial de Aranjuez se dispone a detener a un hombre peligroso y armado que se ha fugado y que alardea de querer matar a los agentes que le quieran detener.
A 35 km de Santo Domingo, en la cárcel de la Victoria, 'Encarcelados' busca a siete españoles presos. Es la primera vez que una televisión extranjera accede al penal más grande del país.

Jalis de la Serna se desplaza hasta Bolivia, un país en el que cumplen condena 70 españoles por traficar droga. El reportero entra en la cárcel de San Sebastián, en Cochabamba, donde hay cuatro españoles entre los 800 presos.
Alejandra Andrade entra en la única cárcel de mujeres de Costa Rica y en La Reforma, el centro penitenciario más grande y peligroso del país centroamericano.

Luisa Moragón falleció en extrañas circunstancias el día que iban a darle el alta. El cuadro clínico de lo más extraño puso en alerta al personal del hospital y a la policía y los hizo cuestionarse si habría un ángel de la muerte entre sus paredes.
En diciembre de 2019, Beatriu Friginal denunció ante la policía la desaparición en misteriosas circunstancias de su marido, Isaac Guillén, una persona aquejada de una enfermedad.

En febrero de 2019, Jesús María Baranda, vecino de Castro Urdiales, desaparece sin dejar rastro. Su cabeza, guardada en una caja, fue entregada por la principal sospechosa a una amiga, que no la abrió hasta meses después.

Los reporteros del programa documentan un caso sin resolver: el brutal asesinato de Antonio Quesada y Ana María Artiles, un matrimonio de jubilados de Las Palmas. Doce años después, la justicia da un giro inesperado.

Shein y Temu, las dos grandes plataformas de comercio chino online, han revolucionado la forma de comprar. Los gigantes asiáticos consiguen vender a precios muy bajos. Los reporteros del programa abordan el lado oscuro del ultra low cost.
Tres tiros acabaron con la vida de Iván Castro, un mecánico asturiano de 31 años al que mataron a bocajarro en el garaje donde aparcaba su coche.

Las leyendas españolas describen a muchos seres sobrenaturales: vampiros, brujas, hombres lobo, tibicenas y perros fantasmales. Aunque son criaturas imposibles, muchos testigos aseguran haberse topado con alguna de ellas en un mal día.

El Arca de la Alianza, el Santo Grial o la Mesa de Salomón son solo algunos objetos a los que se les atribuye cierto poder. Por esta razón, han sido codiciados por mucha gente a lo largo de la historia: desde Constantino hasta Hitler.

La Iglesia es una vieja institución que guarda grandes misterios. Los ejemplos son muchos y van desde la identidad de la persona que aparece en la Sábana Santa, hasta hechos vinculados a la figura del demonio y los exorcismos.

¿Quién no ha fantaseado con recibir una herencia de un pariente que hizo las Américas? Jalis de la Serna busca al heredero de Antonio, un peluquero de origen gallego que falleció en Miami, EEUU, dejando un patrimonio de casi un millón de euros.

Jalis de la Serna acompaña a Pablo, uno de los cazadores más veteranos del equipo, en la búsqueda del heredero de dos apartamentos con vistas al mar en Torremolinos, valorados en 250.000 euros. Solo hay un inconveniente: los pisos están okupados.

After high school graduation, Andy Hardy (Mickey Rooney) reconsiders going on to college to follow in the footsteps of his father, Judge James Hardy (Lewis Stone). Persuading his parents to allow him to spend the summer in New York City, Andy drives there with wealthy friend Betsy Booth (Judy Garland). Unable to find a job immediately, Andy lets his small allowance be taken by a gold digger, but he writes home that all is well. After Betsy finds Andy sleeping in a park, she reports to the judge.

Private detectives Wolf J. Flywheel, Wacky and Ravelli (The Marx Brothers) are hired by the officious Martha Phelps (Margaret Dumont), co-owner of the Phelps Department Store. Her beloved nephew, Tommy (Tony Martin), has been assaulted, shortly after he announced plans to sell his share of the store. Unbeknownst to Martha, the culprit is her fiancé, sleazy store manager Mr. Grover (Douglas Dumbrille), who wants Tommy dead before the sale exposes his years of fraud and theft.

In 1872, Dodge City, Kansas was the epicenter of cattle drives and lawlessness. Run by Jeff Surrett (Bruce Cabot), Dodge City isn't safe for anyone or anything. When Wade Hatton (Errol Flynn) arrives for a cattle drive, he's moved by the violent death of a young boy to take up the post of sheriff and take back the town from Surrett and his cohorts. But first he must contend with the rowdy townsfolk who, having been so long without law, desire to take the law into their own hands.

At a luxurious Berlin hotel between the wars, the once-wealthy Baron Felix von Gaigern (John Barrymore) supports himself as a thief and gambler. In this lavish adaptation of the successful Broadway play, the baron romances one of his marks, the aging ballerina Grusinskaya (Greta Garbo), and teams with dying accountant Otto Kringelein (Lionel Barrymore) against his former boss, crooked industrialist Preysing (Wallace Beery), and his ambitious stenographer, Flaemmchen (Joan Crawford).

Charismatic gambler John McCabe (Warren Beatty) arrives in a mining community and decides to open a brothel. The local residents are impressed by his confident demeanor and fast talk, but crafty prostitute Constance Miller (Julie Christie) sees through McCabe's words and realizes he isn't as sharp as he seems. For a share in his profits, Mrs. Miller agrees to help plan and run McCabe's establishment, but soon a powerful company threatens to destroy what they have built up.

While investigating a series of mysterious deaths, Sergeant Ben Peterson (James Whitmore) finds a young girl (Sandy Descher) who is unable to speak. As Peterson joins forces with FBI agent Robert Graham (James Arness) and scientist Dr. Harold Medford (Edmund Gwenn), he discovers that all the incidents are due to giant ants that have been mutated by atomic radiation. Peterson and Graham, with the aid of the military, attempt to find the queen ants and destroy the nests before the danger spreads.

In Berlin in 1931, American cabaret singer Sally Bowles (Liza Minnelli) meets British academic Brian Roberts (Michael York), who is finishing his university studies. Despite Brian's confusion over his sexuality, the pair become lovers, but the arrival of the wealthy and decadent playboy Maximilian von Heune (Helmut Griem) complicates matters for them both. This love triangle plays out against the rise of the Nazi party and the collapse of the Weimar Republic.

During the 1850s, Milly (Jane Powell), a pretty young cook, marries Adam (Howard Keel), a grizzled woodsman, after a brief courtship. When the two return to Adam's farm, Milly is shocked to meet his six ill-mannered brothers, all of whom live in his cabin. She promptly begins teaching the brothers proper behavior, and most importantly, how to court a woman. But after the brothers kidnap six local girls during a town barn-raising, a group of indignant villagers tries to track them down.

Socialite Judith Traherne (Bette Davis) lives a lavish but emotionally empty life. Riding horses is one of her few joys, and her stable master (Humphrey Bogart) is secretly in love with her. Told she has a brain tumor by her doctor, Frederick Steele (George Brent), Judith becomes distraught. After she decides to have surgery to remove the tumor, Judith realizes she is in love with Dr. Steele, but more troubling medical news may sabotage her new relationship, and her second chance at life.

Without a candidate to run for the senate seat against admired Republican Crocker Jarmon (Don Porter), campaign manager Marvin Lucas (Peter Boyle) recruits leftist lawyer Bill McKay (Robert Redford). McKay's appearance piques the public's interest, and gradually Lucas pushes McKay toward a more centrist message. As McKay's original and honest platform gets watered down, his popularity increases so much that he is running even with Jarmon as Election Day approaches.

On a sea voyage to transport breadfruit to Jamaica, English Captain Bligh (Trevor Howard) abuses his crew and officers enough to anger his 1st Lieutenant, Fletcher Christian (Marlon Brando). When they reach their destination, tensions ease and the crew luxuriates in island life until Bligh claps several men in irons for trying to desert. On the trip home, further indignities inspire Christian to stage a mutiny and set Bligh and those loyal to him afloat in a row boat.

In this sci-fi classic, a spacecraft travels to the distant planet Altair IV to discover the fate of a group of scientists sent there decades earlier. When Commander John J. Adams and his crew arrive, they discover only two people: Dr. Morbius and his daughter, Altaira, who was born on the remote planet. Soon, Adams begins to uncover the mystery of what happened on Altair IV, and why Morbius and Altaira are the sole survivors.
